notes: Board of Park Commissioners minutes, September 1922 to December 1923. Curated: Kezar Stadium's beginnings, the de Young extension, Mountain Lake Park's dedication, the Steinhart Aquarium's dedication.

coverage.remaining: Not placed (no page): Harding Park named for President Harding on the Spring Valley land at Lake Merced, its golf links by William Watson, the Herbert Fleishhacker Playfield naming, Christine Breon's gateway at 19th Avenue and Lincoln Way, Aquatic Park plans by Bakewell and Brown, Clarence Ward's playground buildings at Sloat Boulevard, a tea room in the Fleishhacker bathhouse by Ward & Blohme, the Rideout bequest, a golf caddy house by Kelham (course not named).
coverage.note: Dated by the 'At a regular meeting ... held ... <weekday>, <date>' opener; the meeting of December 21, 1922 was postponed. Curated list PB1922.py.

findings.address_as_written: Extension of the M. H. de Young Memorial Museum
findings.description: The Board of Park Commissioners gratefully accepted M. H. de Young's offer to build at his own expense, and give the city, an extension of the M. H. de Young Memorial Museum.

citation.label: Minutes of the Board of Park Commissioners, November 16, 1922

raw.text: Extension of the M. H. de Young Memorial Museum

findings.address_as_written: Kezar bequest; plans for the new stadium
findings.description: Under its agreement with the executors of Mary A. Kezar, the Board of Park Commissioners settled that her memorial would be an oval and stadium on the part of Golden Gate Park then given to flower beds and stables, to be called Recreation Field, and authorized the architect Willis Polk and the structural engineer Shirley Baker to prepare its plans and estimate, without charge unless it was built.
